This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: In patients with cirrhosis, bumetanide—a loop diuretic with an acidic sulfonamide/arylamine scaffold—had absolute oral bioavailability of 95% (1 mg oral vs IV, n=8), providing direct same-condition, same-class support for high F.
Tolfenamic acid in alcoholic cirrhosis had oral bioavailability of about 100% (100 mg p.o. vs i.v., AUC comparison), another cirrhosis-context record well above the 20% threshold.
Isradipine in cirrhosis had systemic availability of about 37% (36.9 ± 16.2%), still above the 20% threshold, so even the least-absorbed cirrhosis record does not support F < 20%.

The query's physicochemical prior (fully ionized, logD -0.84, TPSA 100) is a concern but not affirmative evidence of F < 20%; the closest transferable record is an acidic, ionized loop diuretic with F = 95% in the same condition.

Query-specific permeability, solubility, and first-pass extraction are not experimentally measured; the low prior is physicochemical only.
Cirrhosis severity and the query's formulation/dose are unspecified; L1 cirrhosis records used different doses and formulations.
Transfer from bumetanide/tolfenamic acid/isradipine relies on structural and condition analogy rather than identical-molecule data.
